Use the left and right keys to choose your stance, then set the angle, power, and spin intensity to complete the throw. The greater the power, the less any spin will affect the trajectory. This makes it easier to score a strike, and harder for pins to alter the balls trajectory.
Each game has 3 frames, with 2 throws per frame. <color=#FFC63D>Each pin knocked down scores 1 point</color>.

<color=#FFFFFF>Strike</color>: Knock down all pins in one throw, scoring 10 points. <color=#FFC63D>The scores from the next two throws</color> are added to this frame’s total. <color=#FFFFFF>Spare</color>: Knock down all pins in two throws, scoring 10 points. <color=#FFC63D>The next throw’s score is added</color> to this frame’s total.

In the final frame, if the first two throws result in a strike or spare, the player earns a <color=#FFC63D>Bonus Throw</color>. All three throws in this frame are tallied directly, with a maximum of 30 points. <color=#FFC63D>No bonus carries forward.</color>
There are 10 splits in total, with 3 chances to fail. Upon completing the challenge, your score is calculated based on the total number of split pins that were knocked down.

A game originating from Chongxiao. Four players compete at one table, forming sets through Pong and Kong and scoring points by winning hands (Hu). The game does not end on Hu — it continues until all tiles are drawn, with the highest total score winning.

Back to Longqi, that bucolic tea town in Chongxiao dotted with white-walled buildings and black tiled-roofs. The rice cakes you loved as a kid, and the Broadcast Goose that used to chase you into the pond, are just the way you left them.
Take a stroll and challenge Mr. Li to a round of chess under the old camphor tree, roast up a fresh batch of tea for your friends to try, or swing by the market to see what fun new finds are waiting.

Bid a brief farewell to Nova City and return to Chongxiao.
Amid the misty, rain-veiled hills of Longqi, a girl named Yinglong approaches a turning point in her life.

Two players take turns rolling.

Your turn: Roll #cfa762e6 dice#z (this can be increased to 8 through Badges), then review the results; #cfa762ekeep any number of dice you wish#z, then #cfa762ereroll the remaining dice#z.

At the start of a round, one player rolls 6 dice (This can be increased to 8 using a Chaos Bottle Cap). After checking the results, you may #cfa762ekeep any number of dice and reroll the rest#z.

Special rules:

If #cfa762ethe rerolled dice#z form a valid combo or include #cfa762ea lone 1 or 6#z, you may once again #cfa762ekeep some dice and reroll the remaining dice#z (you must keep at least 1 dice each time). If neither of these conditions are met, you bust and score 0 for that round. If#cfa762eyou get down to one final die#z and #cfa762eroll a 1 or 6#z (a lucky overload), you do not go bust — your points are added to your total score and you gain one #cfa762eextra turn#z (this can occur consecutively).

At the end of the round, the scores are tallied #cfa762e#z: Score = (sum of the dice) × (sum of the combo multipliers). The first player to reach the target score wins!
